clue.text: Phil's in pieces going over lines

definitions.note: the surname belonging to Phil, the drummer and singer of Genesis

indicators.note: the coins are placed over and around the lines, so they enclose them

parts.note: pieces are coins, as in pieces of eight
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines

explanation.surface: Someone called Phil has gone to pieces over some lines, perhaps forgotten ones on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Phil Collins is the famous Phil, so his surname is what is meant by Phil's.

clue.text: Arrive at party and face problem

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a party and has to face up to a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackhead, a skin blemish usually on the face, is the medical sense.

clue.text: Girl entertains a name over in folly

indicators.note: the girl takes in the turned letters as a host takes in guests

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name

indicators.note: over means the letters are turned back

explanation.surface: A girl puts up a guest over a name, which is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extreme foolishness, madness in action.

clue.text: One of the originators, possibly, but no hero

definitions.text: One of the originators, possibly, but no hero

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be rearranged, once the hero has been taken from them

explanation.surface: One who starts trouble may be among the originators of a scheme, yet earns no praise.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ORIGINATORS less the letters of HERO ('but no hero') leaves letters that rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs up and starts trouble is a ringleader, one of its originators but hardly admirable.

clue.text: Writer's filling issue for singer and playwright

indicators.note: the writer's word fills the gap inside the issue

parts.note: a son is issue, offspring
the writer's is I'm, I am, the setter speaking

explanation.surface: A writer is fleshing out an issue for a musician and dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Simon the singer-songwriter and Neil Simon the playwright share this surname.

clue.text: He beats stranger after dreadful start

indicators.note: the start of the word dreadful is just its opening letter

parts.note: rummer is a British comparative of rum, meaning odd or strange

explanation.surface: A man beats a stranger after a dreadful beginning to some encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is British slang for odd, so 'stranger' gives RUMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist is someone who beats skins and cymbals for a living.

clue.text: Strand grass for sand hopper

parts.note: to desert someone is to strand them
to rat or grass is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: A strand of beach grass for a small hopping creature of the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' and 'grass' look like beach nouns but are verbs. A sand hopper is really a beach creature, so the definition misleads too.
explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa, a small rodent that leaps across arid sands, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: One needing exercise wants female

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so the letter for female is missing

parts.note: unfit means out of condition, needing exercise

explanation.surface: A man who needs to get fit says he wants a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thing, a number one, is a single item or quantity.

clue.text: Bloke's endlessly reckless language

parts.note: a bloke is a man; the s is the link is

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: daring means bold, reckless

explanation.surface: A man's endlessly reckless language, that is his swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief form of Chinese, spoken in Beijing, is a language.

clue.text: Soldiers rush to load batteries again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
to charge is to rush at

explanation.surface: Soldiers rush forward to reload the gun batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: Batteries look like artillery in the surface; the definition means power cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting power back into cells or a phone is to top them up once more.

clue.text: Deprived of minibus not in the same place

indicators.note: not says the minibus is to be without the following letters

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, is Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes

explanation.surface: Someone is deprived of a minibus that is not where it was left.
explanation.walkthrough: IB (ibidem) is the footnote abbreviation for 'in the same place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean lacking or without, as in being three players short or without them.

clue.text: Fervent disorder with Paisley, perhaps, in charge

parts.note: a mess is a disorder or muddle
Ian Paisley was a Northern Irish preacher and politician; perhaps marks him as one Ian

explanation.surface: A fervent ruckus breaks out with the preacher Ian Paisley in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley, a fiery Northern Ireland preacher and politician, makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous devotion to a cause, like that of a saviour's followers, is what both words describe.

clue.text: Journal covering leaderless lawsuit's volume of words

indicators.note: the journal wraps around the shortened lawsuit

parts.note: a diary is a journal

indicators.note: the lawsuit loses its leader, that is its first letter

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A legal journal reports on a lawsuit brought without a lead plaintiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a reference book listing and explaining the words of a language.

clue.text: Masters Genesis number

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, so two masters give two of them
the second MA of the two masters

explanation.surface: Masters golfers might count the number of a hole in Genesis, or count chapters.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is the rock band, not the book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Mama is a 1983 hit single by the rock band Genesis, so it is one of their songs.

clue.text: They check cards and figures on green flags

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on the other, the figures alongside the flag

parts.note: a pin is the flagstick on a golf green
numbers are figures

explanation.surface: Golf scorecards are checked, figures written alongside the flags on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: On a golf course the 'pin' is the flagstick in the hole on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal identification codes confirm that a bank card is being used by its owner.

clue.text: IRA's grit seen to emerge from this event?

definitions.text: IRA's grit seen to emerge from this event?

indicators.note: the letters come out of the mix in a new order

parts.note: the possessive s is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: Irish republican determination is said to have grown out of a historic uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The Easter Rising was the 1916 rebellion in Dublin against British rule, from which later Irish republicanism grew.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1916 Dublin rebellion is the event from which republican resolve emerged.

clue.text: Hesitant but alert, relegating leading pair

indicators.note: the two opening letters are sent down to a lower place in the word

parts.note: attentive means alert

explanation.surface: A player is hesitant but alert after the top two in the league are relegated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relegating leading pair' moves AT, the first two letters, further down the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone uncertain, not yet committed.

clue.text: Mark to remain a long time confined in flats, typically

indicators.note: the long time is shut inside the proofreading mark

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: A mark shows a long stay by someone confined in flats.
explanation.walkthrough: Flats are painted canvas screens used as theatre scenery, not apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre scenery is built from flats, so they are an example of the scenery.

clue.text: Rum compound made out of rare fluid

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A rum mixture is made from a rare liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum from Guyana, named after the region, is the spirit meant.

clue.text: He makes cheeky revelation in Times about English novel

indicators.note: the man and his rude display sit inside the two times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, doubled for times
taken as written
moons means bares the buttocks as a prank
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man bares his bottom in a newspaper story about England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is two Ts. To moon is to show one's bare buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins wrote this 1868 book, often called the first detective story in English.

clue.text: Spacecraft left in a swimming pool

indicators.note: the letter for left is put inside the jumbled pool
swimming suggests the letters of pool are moving about

explanation.surface: Someone left in a swimming pool, as if floating in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns POOL into POLO; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's moon missions used the craft named after the Greek god.

clue.text: The way things are, wine's flooding Italy

indicators.note: the wine spreads round the letter for Italy as a flood surrounds land

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine; the s is kept
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: That is how it is: Italian wine is pouring all over Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state, without change.

clue.text: See 24
Masterpiece of gun surgery by American

parts.note: a magnum is a powerful handgun
an op is an operation, surgery

explanation.surface: A gunshot wound is repaired by an American surgeon in a masterly operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for great work, the phrase names an artist's finest achievement.

clue.text: Lots light up, beginning to drink

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: neon is a kind of light

indicators.note: the beginning of drink is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lots of people light up as soon as they start drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, an endless amount, is a colloquial way to say a great many.

clue.text: Party's feeling agitated about answer

indicators.note: the stirred letters go around the letter for answer
agitated means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: The party is feeling uneasy about its response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges FEELING to go around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine Gael is a centre-right political party in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Steady second independent Liberal returned in contested seat

indicators.note: the turned-round group goes inside the jumbled seat
contested suggests the seat is fought over and its letters thrown about
returned says the run of letters is read backwards

explanation.surface: An election report: a steady second place for an independent, with a Liberal re-elected in a marginal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SILIB into BILIS, which goes inside ESTA, the anagram ('contested') of SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To steady something is to make it firm and keep it from wobbling.

clue.text: Key to apartment No 5?

parts.note: E is the fifth letter of the alphabet
a flat is an apartment

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the key to flat number five.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical key, the major or minor scale on the note a semitone below E natural.

clue.text: Hunk goes over to relax, say, in swingers' bar

indicators.note: goes over means turns back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a part is a hunk or piece

indicators.note: say marks a word spoken to give a near-spelling

parts.note: to ease is to relax

explanation.surface: A muscular man heads over to unwind in a bar for swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunk' wants to be a handsome man; it is just a piece. 'swingers' bar' is a bar for acrobats, not a nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus acrobats swing from this horizontal bar hung on two ropes.

clue.text: Such rulers stop seditious faction after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution the run of letters faces the other way
a faction is a part, so only a part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Tyrannical rulers crush a rebel faction once the revolution is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faction' takes SED, a part of 'seditious'; with STOP that is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrants and autocrats are rulers with absolute power, often cruel.
